title: Agile is Dead • Pragmatic Dave Thomas • GOTO 2015
summary: Dave Thomas argues 'Agile' as a noun has become a fear-driven industry of certifications and scaling frameworks; reclaim agility as small steps, feedback and easy-to-change designs.

assertions.quote: the industry that sprung up around that Manifesto wanted to sell you things

verdicts.note: A historical and framing claim about an industry, not a measurable outcome.

assertions.quote: no rules are Universal fact every rule requires a context

verdicts.note: A philosophical framing of practice advice rather than a testable prediction.

The review concludes agile methods are not necessarily the best choice for large projects, found XP hard to introduce in a complex organisation yet easy elsewhere, and advises practitioners to compare their project's characteristics with each method's required characteristics.

assertions.quote: I think about that as I'm coding and the test doesn't have to exist it still drives the design

verdicts.note: Self-reported by experienced practitioners; no study separates the design effect of TDD from the habit it builds.

assertions.quote: they now have this total bigotry about testing

verdicts.note: A claim about community culture and tone, not a measurable effect.

assertions.quote: it appeals to a corporation because it's got little cute figures and it looks very complicated

verdicts.note: No controlled evidence either way on SAFe-style frameworks; adopter surveys are mixed and self-reported.

assertions.quote: a good design is easier to change than a bad design

verdicts.note: A definition and design heuristic rather than a prediction.

assertions.quote: take a small step forward see where that got you and then revise your plan and repeat

verdicts.note: Practice advice; iterative feedback loops are the shared basis of all agile methods.

Short, uniform development cycles were the factors associated with better quality and productivity while the prescribed test-first order was not, supporting small steps over rule-following, but only for short-term workshop tasks by 39 professionals.

assertions.quote: they end up getting stuck in this process where they don't actually know why they're doing what they're doing

verdicts.note: Plausible and consistent with cargo-cult reports, but no study links certification length to team outcomes.
